newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ATHLETICS-BAILEY UNCONCERNED BY LAUSANNE DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAILEY UNCONCERNED BY LAUSANNE DEFEAT.

text.p: Newly-crowned American champion Maurice Greene sent an intimidating warning to Olympic champion Donovan Bailey before next month's world championships when he beat the Canadian in a high-class 100 metres on Wednesday.

Despite pouring rain at the Lausanne grand prix meeting, Greene came through strongly in the final 10 metres to hold off Olympic silver medallist Frankie Fredericks and Bailey to win in 9.90 seconds, equalling his own second fastest time in the world this year.

Bailey, who finished third, immediately played down the defeat but admitted he had finished badly. There was no sign of the devastating final burst which swept the towering Canadian to the 100 metres title at last year's Atlanta Olympics.
"My last 40 metres was pathetic at best. But I'm not worried. My first 60 has improved dramatically," he said. "I'm not worried about anybody that's here. Technically I know what went wrong."
The field was one of the fastest ever assembled outside of an Olympic or world championship final. Six of the eight sprinters had run under 10 seconds already this season.
The race included six of the finalists at last year's Atlanta Olympics and all three medallists -- Bailey, Fredericks and Ato Boldon of Trinidad.

Greene was pushed all the way, Fredericks taking second only one hundreth of a second behind in 9.91 with Bailey third in 9.97. Britain's former world and Olympic champion Linford Christie could only finish seventh in 10.12. Boldon was sixth in 10.08.

After winning the U.S. title last month -- also in 9.90 seconds -- Greene warned that it was time for an American to take control of the world of sprinting. After Wednesday's performance his rivals will have to take him very seriously indeed.

"I felt the world record could have gone with such a field. But I just went into the race trying to feel relaxed," he said. "This has given me a lot of confidence for Athens. I think I can do very well there."
In the women's 100 metres, Gail Devers, who missed the U.S. trials because of injury, bounced back by beating American champion Marion Jones in 10.89, the fastest time in the world this year.
Devers just dipped ahead of Jones, who finished one hundreth of a second behind. At the moment Devers cannot go to the world championships because she missed the U.S. trials and was not selected.
But the American could still compete in the 100 hurdles if athletics chiefs decide to give wild cards to defending champions, as is now expected.
World and Olympic high-hurdles champion Allen Johnson also defied the wet conditions to clock the fastest time in the world this year in the men's 110 metres hurdles -- 13.17 seconds.

Despite striking the third hurdle from the finish, Johnson powered through to win ahead of American Olympic silver medallist Mark Crear (13.21) and Cuban Anier Garcia (13.27). Britain's world record holder Colin Jackson was fourth in 13.28.
Sweden's Olympic champion Ludmila Engquist also clocked an impressive 12.65 seconds for the women's 100 metres hurdles, the second fastest time of the season.
